cells.tense: You are here at the desk and the thing you are working with has come whole.
cells.act: spend an hour with the thing you love without a task attached to it
cells.ask: Give an hour to something you love with no task on it. No notes, no improvements, no next version. Half an hour counts if that's what you've got.
cells.core:
When a thing has come whole, you can feel it. That is what makes the structures you set hold — you are not guessing at the edges, you have been near them. The reading and the building run together in you, and the desk is where both get to sit down.

From here the pressure goes the other way: seal it, lock the form, make it hold so it does not have to be touched again. That is not structure, that is a wall. What has come whole is still yours to be near without managing it. Give an hour to something you love and attach nothing to it. Holding a thing without fixing it is not neglect. The pattern stays alive because you can sit in it.
cells.sheetLine: What is whole does not need sealing.
cells.verb: reaching the wholeness of a thing and feeling the whole of what it is
cells.place: at the desk where you decide what holds and what gets put together

cells.tense: You will have finished it in your head long before it has started.
cells.act: define the seed of what will be built, in one line
cells.ask: Before you start the next thing, write one line naming what it is for. Just the line. Then leave the day alone.
cells.core:
The end is already in your head, fully formed, and it pulls the present out from under the work. Steps feel like rehearsal for something better that has not happened. The drive to arrive is real, and it is the same drive that makes your structure hold; tonight it has outrun the thing itself and left the middle of the work thin.

Naming what a thing is for takes a minute and gives it somewhere to stand. Take the next thing and before you touch it, write one line: what it is for. Not what it will look like, not the verdict at the end. Just what it serves. One line, and then the day is yours. The line can change tomorrow, and if it does, that was still a choice and not a compulsion.

cells.tense: You stood at the door of something whole, and you are still standing there in the past.
cells.act: begin the thing while it is still nothing in particular
cells.ask: Bring something new into being without a plan, a name, or a reason. Start it while it's formless and see what it wants to become.
cells.core:
The wholeness is doing its work from behind a pane of glass. You can see the shape a thing took once it was set, and it sits back there while you stand where you are, not quite arriving at anything ahead of you. The setting and the fitting are still in you. Nothing is asking them for anything.

It does not come back by trying harder. Begin the thing while it is still nothing in particular — no purpose, no form, no name. Say yes before the case has been made to you. The spark does not need structure around it. What it needs is for you to move before the deciding.

cells.tense: You are setting the structure right now, and you file it under how things tend to work.
cells.act: let the inner compass decide the small case
cells.ask: When something feels off among people and nobody names it — let the compass decide. Say it, adjust it, or move it. Then done.
cells.core:
The work of making something whole — deciding what fits, what is fair, where the seam belongs — is running, and the account you give of it is that the situation sorted itself. Your hands are on the pattern while the pattern gets described as something that settles by itself. That is the whole gap: the doing is real, and the name you give it is thinner than the doing.

For one small case where something feels off in a group and nobody says so, let what you feel about it decide. Say the thing, adjust the thing, move the thing. Then let it close and go unreviewed. Standing beside your own reading is not a speech and needs no witnesses; it is enough that the compass is counted as yours when it moves.
